name: Icelandic
catalog_quote: Stress falls on the initial syllable. Secondary stress on odd numbered syllables thereafter.
sweep_summary: The single sweep item (Hildebrandt 1963) is a Hamburg dissertation on vowel duration in the North Low Saxon dialect of Wewelsfleth; Glottolog's own reference page shows the Icelandic link is a computerized mis-assignment from the word 'zugleich'. Irrelevant to Icelandic, not fetched sources, priority none.hi.is) were downloaded (2013 Hljóðkerfi og orðhlutakerfi íslensku, 1990 Íslensk hljóðfræði, 1993 Íslensk hljóðkerfisfræði, 1984 Íslensk málfræði) and saved with under The 2013 edition §5.2 pp. 47-48 gives a first-hand statement: primary stress on the first syllable; rhythmic secondary stress on the 3rd/5th/7th syllable in simplex words (kennari [ˈcʰɛnːaˌrɪ]), but inherent root stress wins in compounds (kennarastofa [ˈcʰɛnːaraˌstɔːva]; alþingismaður with a second main stress). This confirms the catalog's fixed-initial coding and refines its 'secondary stress on odd-numbered syllables' clause; it is proposed as the new deciding source in place of the second-hand one-sentence summary in Flego & Berkson 2020. Árnason 1985 (Wiley 403), Árnason 2011 ch. 13 (OUP 403), Liberman 1975 (De Gruyter 405) and Einarsson 1949 (archive.org lending-restricted) remain unread; Árnason 1985/2011 stay the high-priority acquisitions.

new_statements.quote: Meginreglan um orðáherslu í íslensku er sú að aðaláhersla fellur á fyrsta atkvæði orðs. Það er oftast rót, en getur einnig verið forskeyti. [...] En einnig er sterk tilhneiging til að setja aukaáherslu á öll atkvæði sem ekki standa við hliðina á áhersluatkvæðum. Þessi tilhneiging veldur því að aukaáhersla leitast við að koma á þriðja (fimmta, sjöunda o.s.frv.) atkvæði og leiðir því til víxlhrynjandi þar sem áhersluatkvæði og áherslulaus skiptast á. Orðið kennari yrði því með áherslutáknum hljóðritað [ˈcʰɛnːaˌrɪ]. Aftur á móti kemur ekki aukaáhersla á þriðja atkvæði í orðinu kennarastofa vegna þess að það stendur við hliðina á rótaratkvæði.
new_statements.translation: The main rule of word stress in Icelandic is that primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word. That is usually a root, but can also be a prefix. [...] But there is also a strong tendency to put secondary stress on every syllable that does not stand next to a stressed syllable. This tendency makes secondary stress seek the third (fifth, seventh, etc.) syllable and thus leads to alternating rhythm in which stressed and unstressed syllables alternate. The word kennari would therefore be transcribed with stress marks as [ˈcʰɛnːaˌrɪ]. By contrast, no secondary stress falls on the third syllable of kennarastofa, because it stands next to a root syllable.
new_statements.citation: Eiríkur Rögnvaldsson. 2013. Hljóðkerfi og orðhlutakerfi íslensku. Reykjavík: author's open edition (preface dated 25 Nov 2013), 192 pp. §5.2 'Áhersla og hrynjandi', pp. 47-48.
new_statements.reading: First-hand statement by an Icelandic phonologist: primary stress is fixed on the initial syllable (root or prefix); secondary stress on odd-numbered syllables is a rhythmic tendency, not an exceptionless rule — it is overridden by inherent root stress in compounds (kennarastofa takes secondary stress on the 4th syllable, [ˈcʰɛnːaraˌstɔːva]), while in compounds with a monosyllabic first member rhythm wins (háskóli [ˈhauːskouˌlɪ]); multi-member compounds often carry a further main stress on the last member's root (alþingismaður [ˈalþiɲcɪsˈmaːðʏr]); a prefix can lose its stress in connected speech (óvitlaus). This confirms the catalog's 'fixed-strict' initial coding and refines the secondary-stress clause: odd-syllable rhythm holds for simplex words, root stress wins in compounds.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding Flego & Berkson 2020:10 sentence is verbatim in the held text at the stated page; the StressTyp2 dq is verbatim in the held StressTyp2 dump (passages 1091/1092); the Dehé 2009:5-6 corroboration was not held, so I fetched sources the open KOPS postprint and confirmed it verbatim, including Árnason's 1985:94 examples printed ˈkennarˌanum (Swsw) and ˈhamarˌinn (Sws). Three independent secondary sources agree on initial main stress plus rhythmic secondary stress on odd-numbered syllables, and Dehé's reproduction of Árnason's trisyllable with final secondary stress supports the '101' cell that our 'corr' note flags as analysis-dependent (Hayes 1995 reads it as final lengthening). sources.note: Initial main stress; in trisyllabic and longer words odd-numbered syllables carry secondary stress and even-numbered are weak (citing Árnason 1985); prefixes such as ó- and some derivational suffixes alter the pattern (Árnason 1987, Bergsveinsson 1963).

sources.note: Main stress on the first syllable of the word (usually the root, but also a prefix). Secondary stress is of two kinds: rhythmic stress, which tends to land on the 3rd (5th, 7th...) syllable giving alternating rhythm (kennari [ˈcʰɛnːaˌrɪ]), and inherent root stress; in kennarastofa the 3rd syllable gets no secondary stress because it is adjacent to a root syllable, which takes it instead (4th syllable, [ˈcʰɛnːaraˌstɔːva]). In compounds with a monosyllabic first member rhythm wins over root stress (háskóli [ˈhauːskouˌlɪ]); compounds with a polysyllabic first member and multiple compounds often…

sources.citation: Snæbjörn Jónsson. 1927. A Primer of Modern Icelandic. London: Oxford University Press (Humphrey Milford). 'Accent' paragraph.
sources.quote: The accent almost invariably falls on the first syllable, the only exceptions being the negative prefix ó- (un-) when employed with a word which commonly does not take a prefix, as ókotungslegur (=kotungslegur) 'ungenerous' (=mean), óíslenskur 'un-Icelandic', and in certain cases the prefix all- (rather, very) as allfeginn 'rather pleased'. In such cases the accent often falls equally on the two first syllables, or even mainly on the second.
sources.locator: 'Accent' section (djvu text lines 279-289; scanned, page number not recoverable from the text)
sources.note: Accent almost invariably on the first syllable; exceptions are the negative prefix ó- with words that do not normally take a prefix and sometimes the prefix all-, where accent falls equally on the first two syllables or even mainly on the second. Nothing on secondary stress.

Sú tilhneiging til víxlhrynjandi, sem áður var nefnd, veldur því svo að aukaáhersla (sem táknuð er með [ˌ]) leitast við að koma á þriðja (fimmta, sjöunda o.s.frv.) atkvæði.
